title: Tensor cohomology segments and quantitative Tor bounds for a pro-etale triangle
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and $A$ an arbitrary commutative ring. Work on the small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with its constant sheaf of rings $A_Y$ and the unbounded derived category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Use the K-flat derived tensor product [def-weil-derived-tensor] and cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $U\to V\to W\to U[1]$ be a distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For every degree-zero $A_Y$-module sheaf $N$ and every $i\in\mathbf Z$, its tensor image has an exact cohomology segment
$$
 \mathcal H^i(U\otimes_A^L N)\longrightarrow
 \mathcal H^i(V\otimes_A^L N)\longrightarrow
 \mathcal H^i(W\otimes_A^L N).
$$
If $U$ has Tor amplitude in $[a_U,b_U]$ and $W$ in $[a_W,b_W]$, where $a_U\leq b_U$ and $a_W\leq b_W$ are integers, then $V$ has Tor amplitude in
$$[\min(a_U,a_W),\max(b_U,b_W)].$$
In particular if both outside vertices have Tor amplitude in the same ordered interval $[a,b]$, the middle vertex has Tor amplitude in exactly that interval. Tor amplitude means the vanishing for every module sheaf in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]; no constructibility or finiteness assumption on the coefficient ring or the vertices is imposed.
